name: Texas

law.summary: Every unauthorized discharge or SSO goes to the TCEQ regional office within 24 hours (written report in 5 working days). A local-government facility must also notify local government officials and local media within 24 hours, but only for spills likely to affect drinking water, 50,000 gallons or more near a water supply or in a recharge zone, or 100,000 gallons or more; nothing requires a web posting.

citations.title: Notification Requirements
citations.quote: The owner of a facility must designate a responsible individual to comply with this subchapter. ... (3) a spill of 100,000 gallons or more.
citations.who: owner of a facility (local government) through its responsible individual
citations.channel: local government officials and local media; hand delivery, fax, email, or phone with written follow-up
citations.deadline: as soon as possible, no later than 24 hours after becoming aware; copy to the TCEQ regional office within 48 hours of the notice
citations.threshold: any spill likely to affect a drinking-water source; 50,000 gallons or more near a source or in a sensitive area; 100,000 gallons or more

citations.title: Notice to Local Officials and Local Media: precautionary statements
citations.quote: (precautionary statements include that the public should) avoid contact with spill material, soil, or water in the affected area

citations.title: Reporting Unauthorized Discharges and SSOs
citations.quote: as soon as possible but no later than 24 hours ... within five working days
citations.channel: TCEQ regional office (phone, in person, fax); after hours 800-832-8224
citations.deadline: 24 hours; 5 working days written; monthly summary for qualifying small spills by the 20th of the next month
citations.threshold: any UD or SSO regardless of volume

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours to the regional office; written within 5 working days; or monthly summary for qualifying small spills

bills_and_cases: No 2025 (89th Legislature) bill on public notice of sewage spills found; SB 565 (2025) amends Water Code 7.0026 (text not read).
2015 HB 2051 / SB 912 and 2013 HB 824 (thresholds and monthly reporting for small spills).
Consent decrees: Houston (2021, 4:18-cv-03368), San Antonio (2013), others not checked.

erule.notes: TCEQ takes reports through its regional offices and STEERS; only 8 Texas events from 5 permits in SOBE.

statewide_feed.latency: one to four months (refreshed in batches; on 2026-11-03 it held reports received to 2026-08-31, refreshed 2026-09-24)
statewide_feed.history: 2010-09 to date (56,545 rows; about 4,000 to 6,000 a year since 2016)
statewide_feed.receiving_water: free text when given (about 59 percent of rows) plus TCEQ river segment code
statewide_feed.license: No licence stated (licenseId null); data.texas.gov terms apply.
statewide_feed.notes: Metadata says 'Update Frequency: Semiannually'; geocoding needed from addresses in incident_description or the regulated entity location.

sso.location_source: none with coordinates; county, address text and regulated entity

beaches.program: Texas Beach Watch (Texas General Land Office; local governments post advisories)
beaches.notes: 174 stations on a public ArcGIS layer with advisory level, last result and date.

habs.program: none for freshwater found; TPWD red tide tracking on the coast

health_department_pages: Galveston County Health District beach water advisories

shared_waters: Red River and Lake Texoma (OK, AR)

barriers.what: The public notice under 30 TAC 319.302 goes to local officials and media only, and only above 100,000 gallons (or 50,000 near water supplies); no web posting.
The TCEQ open dataset lags one to four months and is refreshed in batches; current reports are only in regional files.
barriers.note: Ask TCEQ for a monthly or weekly refresh.

barriers.what: Houston's monthly SSO reports and maps are PDFs.

readiness.rationale: A statewide Socrata table of every reported SSO since 2010 with dates, volume, cause, permit and often the water body, but no coordinates and a lag of months; geocoding is the extra work. Texas Beach Watch is a clean ArcGIS advisory feed.

owner_questions: Accept a one-to-four-month lag for Texas (label 'Dated reports, delayed')?
Geocode SSOs from address text (most rows have a street address in the description) or place them at the plant / county only?
Many rows say 'NO WATER BODY PROVIDED': show them as land spills or only those naming water?
surprise: Texas, with no web-posting duty at all, publishes 56,545 sewer overflow reports since 2010 as an open Socrata dataset (created July 2025), the largest SSO table in this group.
